Question: Let \(S\) be the set of the \(2005\) smallest positive multiples of \(4,\) and let \(T\) be the set of the \(2005\) smallest positive multiples of \(6.\) How many elements are common to \(S\) and \(T?\)
Solution:
A common element must be divisible by both \(4\) and \(6\). Their least common multiple is \(12\), so the common positive multiples are \(12,24,36,\ldots\).

The largest elements of the two sets are
\[
4\cdot2005=8020\quad\text{and}\quad6\cdot2005=12030.
\]
Thus a common element cannot exceed \(8020\). Conversely, every positive multiple of \(12\) at most \(8020\) belongs to both sets, because it is a multiple of each number and lies within both lists.

Now
\[
12\cdot668=8016\le8020<8028=12\cdot669.
\]
Therefore the common elements are exactly \(12\cdot1,12\cdot2,\ldots,12\cdot668\). These are distinct, so there are \(\boxed{668}\) common elements, choice \(\text{D}\).
